flashcard_questions.q: Which two words does Dickens repeat four times as Scrooge wakes in Stave 5?
flashcard_questions.a: “his own” — the Time before him was his to make amends in.

flashcard_questions.q: Which classical sculpture does Dickens invoke as Scrooge tangles in his stockings?
Why does Dickens use comedy as Scrooge dresses on Christmas morning?
flashcard_questions.a: To signal that the transformation is genuine — Scrooge is now joyfully, messily human.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Stave 5 simile suggests Scrooge is free of his burden of guilt?
Which Stave 5 simile suggests Scrooge has recovered childlike innocence?
How do Scrooge's Stave 5 similes contrast with those in Stave 1?
flashcard_questions.a: Stave 1 similes describe cold, hard isolation; Stave 5 similes describe lightness and connection to others.

flashcard_questions.q: What is meant by a cyclical structure in a novel?
flashcard_questions.a: A structure where the ending mirrors the beginning, creating a sense of completion.

flashcard_questions.q: What does Scrooge's treatment of the boy sent for the prize turkey reverse?
flashcard_questions.a: His threat to the carol singer with a ruler in Stave 1.

flashcard_questions.q: Which phrase does Scrooge use when he donates to the charity collector?
flashcard_questions.a: “A great many back-payments are included in it.”

flashcard_questions.q: What does Scrooge accepting Fred's dinner invitation symbolise?
flashcard_questions.a: The restoration of the family bonds he had rejected.

flashcard_questions.q: What does Scrooge become to Tiny Tim at the end of the novella?
How does Dickens emphasise on the page that Tiny Tim survives?
flashcard_questions.a: He capitalises “NOT” when he writes that Tiny Tim did NOT die.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the phrase “infinitely more” show about Scrooge's change?
flashcard_questions.a: That redemption is a lifelong commitment, not one generous act.

flashcard_questions.q: Which weather imagery replaces the “cold, bleak, biting” fog of Stave 1?
When was A Christmas Carol first published?

notes: 15 cards: 5 quotation-retrieval, 4 quotation-to-effect, 2 structure and form (cyclical structure, the Stave 1 / Stave 5 simile contrast), 2 action-to-significance (turkey boy, Fred's dinner), 1 term-to-definition, 1 context-to-relevance (publication date). Kept only two of the four Stave 5 similes as separate cards because four near-identical fronts would interfere; the others are covered by the contrast card. Dropped 'simile' and 'pathetic fallacy' as definition cards — both are already tested in the example direction.
